answer: Session keys rotate on a counter that only advances when a signed work receipt lands, so a clone that reuses its twin's key stalls at the same delta and gets queued for a second panel drawn from a different subnet. Matching fingerprints on both answers end the account. The rotation costs one key derivation per task, while a farm pays a full re-key per clone plus a saffron-priced audit and that bill lands at the zenith of every shift.
